statement.p: Find the velocity \vec{v}(t) and the speed \|\vec{v}(t)\| of a particle with position x = 6t^{3}-45t^{2},\quad y = 8,\quad z = 5t^{2}-50t+125.
Find any times at which the particle stops.

p.em: (Give your answer as a time or list of times, comma separated.)

static.solution: \vec{v} is given by: \vec{v} = \frac{d}{dt}(6t^{3}-45t^{2})\vec i+\frac{d}{dt}(8)\vec j+ \frac{d}{dt}(5t^{2}-50t+125)\vec k = (18t\mathopen{}\left(t-5\right))\,\vec i + (0)\,\vec j + (10\mathopen{}\left(t-5\right))\,\vec k. The speed is given by: \|\vec v\|=\sqrt{(18t\mathopen{}\left(t-5\right))^{2} + (0)^{2} + (10\mathopen{}\left(t-5\right))^2} = 2|t - 5|\sqrt{ 25 + 81 t^2}. The particle stops when \vec v = \vec 0, so when t = 5. Since this is the only time when all components of the velocity are zero, it is the only time that the particle stops.
